subject: Pricing follow-up: committed-use discount & startup program — DeepFin
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ng <alice@deepfin.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-18T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & post-call recap — pricing / committed-use options

Hi Alice — great to chat this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the pricing items we agreed to surface: 

Call highlights:
- DeepFin is planning an initial pilot for the recommendations and summaries product (search + assistant).
- Expected token profile: ~30M tokens/month in month 1-3 (mix of prompt + generations), ramping to ~80M tokens/month by month 6 as more customers onboard.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 400ms for shorter assistant flows; some batch reranking jobs are tolerant to higher latency.

Pricing / unit economics asks (you asked for target numbers):
- Target unit economics you mentioned: want to land around $200–$400 per 1M tokens (target $/1M tokens depends on model choice & quantization).
- Budget range you gave on the call (ballpark): $300k–$500k ARR for inference initially.

Discounts we discussed to consider:
- Startup program (early-stage pricing / credits) — eligibility check (Series A qualifies for our early-stage tier; we can apply a 20–30% startup credit for 12 months).
- Committed-use discounts (monthly/annual commit): tiered model with deeper discounts at higher committed volumes + extra for multi-year commitments.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Draft a committed-use proposal for two scenarios: (A) conservative: 30M tokens/mo commit, 12 months; (B) aggressive: 60–80M tokens/mo, 12–24 months with multi-year pricing.
2) Pull in Ben (pricing lead) and Aditya for approval on any exceptions to standard tiers.
3) Send the pricing sheet + SOW and a DocuSign link for signature if the terms look good.

Can you confirm the following so I model the right tiers?
- Which models are you planning to run in prod (smaller Llama-style vs larger instruction-tuned models)?
- Confirm whether the $300k–$500k ARR is strictly for inference (not including other platform costs).

I’ll have a proposed sheet back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Alice Ng <alice@deepfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@deepfin.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & post-call recap — pricing / committed-use options

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications: 

- Model mix: primarily open models (quantized) for most traffic; 10–20% of traffic will use a larger instruction-tuned model for high-value flows. Assume avg token generation length ~60 tokens.
- Budget: the $300k–$500k ARR is for inference + support/observability. Procurement will want an invoice that separates unit costs vs retained support.
- Startup qualification: DeepFin closed Series A last quarter. Would appreciate details on the startup program level and any usage credits.

For committed-use, finance prefers a firm-year commit (12 months) but will consider 24-month for a better rate. If you can show:
- Scenario 1: 30M tokens/mo commit (12 mo) — price impact
- Scenario 2: 60M tokens/mo commit (12 mo) — price impact
- Scenario 3: 60M tokens/mo commit (24 mo) — multi-year incentive

Also please include any uplift for priority support / SLA. We’ll loop procurement on the next note.

Best,
Alice
Head of Product, DeepFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ng <alice@deepfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-18T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed pricing scenarios (draft)

Alice — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Attached is a draft pricing sheet and a short note on the startup program (attached PDF). High level proposals below (examples modeled from your provided volumes):

List price baseline (for modeling): $385 per 1M tokens (example for the runtimes + model mix you described). Final $/1M varies by model selection and quantization level.

Proposed scenarios (price per 1M tokens after discounts):
- Scenario 1: 30M/mo commit — 20% committed-use discount => $308 / 1M tokens (annualized commit, 12 months).
- Scenario 2: 60M/mo commit — 30% committed-use discount => $269 / 1M tokens (12 months).
- Scenario 3: 60M/mo commit, 24 months — 35% committed-use + 5% multi-year incentive => $238 / 1M tokens (24 months).

Startup program:
- As Series A, DeepFin qualifies for our startup tier: 25% credit applied to list for the first 6 months + a $25k platform credit (observability/support). We can stack startup credit + committed-use discount for an initial blended savings in months 1–6.

Priority support / SLA: +$10k/mo for a named SLA package (24/7 escalation path, 15-minute P0 response, quarterly ROI reviews). We can also include onboarding hours in the first 90 days (2 weeks of engineering support) in the SOW.

Example math (Scenario 2, first year):
- Volume: 60M tokens/mo => 720M tokens/year.
- Price: $269 / 1M => annual inference cost = $269 * 720 = $193,680.
- Apply startup credits (first 6 months 25% credit on list): blended first-year effective spend could drop by another ~$30k depending on exact stacking rules.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm preferred scenario (S1/S2/S3) so I can lock pricing and get a final sign-off from Finance.
2) If you want to proceed, I’ll open an internal pricing exception if we need to go deeper than 35% or modify the startup stacking.
3) I’ll send the SOW + pricing sheet + DocuSign link for signature.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx, startup-discount-terms.pdf

—Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alice Ng <alice@deepfin.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed pricing scenarios (draft)

Looping in to confirm internal approval path. Marissa — the proposed tiers look reasonable to me for a Series A with strong ARR ramp. Two asks before we finalize: 

1) Marissa — please confirm the margin at Scenario 3 (60M/mo, 24 mo, $238 /1M) after expected platform credits and onboarding costs (we need to ensure we meet minimum acceptable margin).
2) Alice — procurement will ask for invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly), PO process, and contract counterparty details. Can you share the procurement contact and any specific PO or W9 requirements?

If both Marissa and Alice greenlight, I’ll approve the pricing exception and hand to finance/legal for contract generation.

Ben
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

- Full SOW and itemized pricing (unit costs separate from support).
- Redlined standard terms (we will return a standard PO; please confirm vendor name and remit address).
- W9 and SOC2 report (if you have a recent SOC2 PDF, attach).

Attached: procurement_form.pdf (we filled preliminary fields)

We plan to route a PO for Scenario 2 (60M/mo, 12 mo) pending receipt of SOW and final contract. Please also share expected invoice cadence.

Thanks,
Procurement Team

Marissa
